You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented

# Outcome sub-dossier — TimkenSteel Corporation realized record, ~3–5-year horizon (fiscal 2018)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed at TimkenSteel's own
> ~3–5-year post-separation record, read from its annual report for fiscal year 2018
> (Form 10-K filed 2019-02-20, accession 0001598428-19-000018). This sub-dossier contains
> no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status in the outcome window
- TimkenSteel Corporation remained an independent SEC registrant with common shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange, filing an annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018 cover page]

## Realized financial trajectory (best-documented outcome scalars)
- For fiscal 2018 the company reported net sales of $1,610.6 million and a net loss of $(31.7) million (basic and diluted loss per share $(0.71)). [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Selected Financial Data]
- The Selected Financial Data table records a net loss in each of the four full fiscal years following the separation and net income in the separation year: net (loss) income of $46.1 million (2014), $(45.0) million (2015), $(105.5) million (2016), $(43.8) million (2017), and $(31.7) million (2018). [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Selected Financial Data]
- Net sales over the same period were $1,674.2 million (2014), $1,106.2 million (2015), $869.5 million (2016), $1,329.2 million (2017), and $1,610.6 million (2018). [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Selected Financial Data]
- Fiscal 2018 net sales rose $281.4 million (21.2%) over 2017; excluding surcharges the increase was $167.4 million (16.1%), attributed to favorable price/mix (approximately $107 million) and higher volumes (approximately $61 million), with ship tons up 49 thousand tons (4.3%) driven by higher demand in industrial and energy end markets, partially offset by a reduction in billet shipments. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, MD&A]
- The fiscal 2018 net loss included a fourth-quarter loss from remeasurement of benefit plans of $43.5 million and a third-quarter executive severance cost of $1.7 million. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Selected Quarterly Financial Data notes]
- The company remained in a valuation-allowance position in 2018 and did not experience a significant reduction in its effective income tax rate or net deferred federal income tax assets from the U.S. tax law changes. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, MD&A]

## Product / process / organization continuity over time
- The company's product line and operations continued along the same lines established at separation: as of fiscal 2018 it manufactured more than 500 grades of high-performance carbon, micro-alloy and alloy steel sold as ingots, bars, tubes and billets, custom-made for industrial, energy and mobile customers, describing this on the basis of its metallurgical expertise and operational capabilities. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Business]
- Workforce: at December 31, 2018 the company had approximately 3,000 employees, with about 61% covered under one of two collective bargaining agreements (expiring December 2019 and September 2021). [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Employment]
- No divestiture, sale, or dissolution of the business was reported in the fiscal 2018 annual report; the company continued to operate the steel business as a going concern. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable in this window
- No documented fracture specifically at the product/process interface (product could not be aligned with operations) or at the process/organization interface (operations vs people/management) was located in the fiscal 2018 annual report beyond the general risk-factor language common to such filings; any such specific disruption is recorded here as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- In its ~3–5-year post-separation window, TimkenSteel remained an independent NYSE-listed going concern operating the same steel product line with a workforce that grew from roughly 2,700 to about 3,000, retained (not divested) its business, and posted a net loss in each of the four full fiscal years 2015–2018 — $(45.0)M, $(105.5)M, $(43.8)M and $(31.7)M — following net income of $46.1 million in the 2014 separation year, with fiscal 2018 net sales recovering to $1,610.6 million on higher industrial and energy demand. [SRC: SEC accession 0001598428-19-000018, Form 10-K FY2018, Selected Financial Data and MD&A]

[SLICE END]
